messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: diff manual
parts:
I guess the diffed manual never got compiled for v1.0.3. I have (as of 69b3db9b006f5d70b3ea147181e8deac4dff20a3) started putting the patch necessary to fix whatever LaTeX errors STAN_HOME/src/docs/stan-reference/diff.sh induces into the STAN_HOME/src/docs/stan-reference/diff_patches directory instead of attaching them to the list. So, now anyone with git, grep, sed, and bash should be able to do from STAN_HOME

./diff_manual.sh v1.0.3. v1.1.0

and upload the manual. I would except I don't have the special fonts so some things look weird and the page numbers are off relative to the plain manual.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] diff manual
parts:
On Thursday, December 20, 2012 2:53:54 AM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
It ran after the most recent pull, but there
seem to be a lot of false negatives on the markup.

False negatives happen for various reasons, but there should be no false positives. Basically, there are a lot of

"no unique match found for: ..."

messages, where it finds a change in a small snippet but refrains from marking that snippet because the same snippet appears multiple times in a file. Maybe this can be improved for future versions, but I sort of hoped that it would at least mark something on a page that had been changed even if it did not mark 100% of the changed lines.

Ben -- did you want me to send you a copy of
the new manual?  Or do you think we should use that
one instead of the un-annotated one?  Now that the
annotations are relatively unintrusive, I wouldn't
mind making this the regular manual.

Maybe attach it, just so that I can make sure it worked as well as it was intended to work. I don't really care if it is an alternative to or a replacement for the plain manual because it should be identical aside from the margins and the last page(s).

Ben
